questions.question_text:
A raffle drum holds $15$ tickets numbered $1$ to $15$, and one is drawn at random.
Let $X$ be the number drawn.
Find $P(X=11)$.

options.why: Used the value $11$ as the numerator instead of the single favourable ticket.
Divided $1$ by the value $11$ rather than by the number of tickets.
Counted the tickets as the $14$ gaps between $1$ and $15$.

questions.solution_text:
The $15$ tickets are equally likely, so $X$ is uniform over $15$ values.
$P(X=11)=\frac{1}{15}$

questions.question_text:
A booklet has $40$ numbered pages. One page number is chosen at random, with all forty page numbers equally likely.
Let $X$ be the page number.
Find $P(X>33)$.

options.why: Included page $33$, although $X>33$ excludes it.
Stopped counting at page $39$, leaving out the last page.
Counted the pages up to $33$ instead of the pages beyond it.

questions.solution_text:
The favourable pages are $34,\ 35,\ \dots,\ 40$, which is $7$ pages.
$P(X>33)=\frac{7}{40}$

questions.question_text:
The random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed over $\{2,\ 6,\ 11,\ 17,\ 23\}$.
Find $P(X\le 11)$.

options.why: Excluded $11$, using $X<11$ instead of $X\le 11$.
Counted only $X=11$ instead of all three values at most $11$.
Treated every integer from $1$ to $23$ as an equally likely value instead of using the five listed values.

questions.solution_text:
Each of the five values has probability $\frac{1}{5}$.
The favourable values are $2,\ 6,\ 11$.
$P(X\le 11)=\frac{3}{5}$

questions.question_text:
The random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed over $\{2,\ 5,\ 8,\ 11,\ 14,\ 17\}$.
Find $P(5\le X<14)$.

options.why: Included $14$, counting four values instead of three.
Excluded $5$, counting only $8$ and $11$.
Used the probability of one value without multiplying by the three favourable values.

questions.solution_text:
Each of the six values has probability $\frac{1}{6}$.
The favourable values are $5,\ 8,\ 11$.
$P(5\le X<14)=\frac{3}{6}$
$=\frac{1}{2}$

questions.question_text:
A bag holds four beads marked $1$, $1$, $2$ and $3$.
One bead is drawn at random and $X$ is the number on it.
Is $X$ uniformly distributed?

options.text: No, because $P(X=1)=\frac{1}{2}$ while $P(X=2)$ and $P(X=3)$ are each $\frac{1}{4}$.
Yes, because one bead is drawn from four, so each has probability $\frac{1}{4}$.
options.why: Gave $\frac{1}{n}$ to the four beads instead of to the three distinct values of $X$.

options.text: Yes, because $X$ has three values, so each has probability $\frac{1}{3}$.
options.why: Assumed any finite set of values is uniform without checking the probabilities.

options.text: No, because the values $1$, $2$ and $3$ are not equally spaced.
options.why: Tested the spacing of the values rather than their probabilities, and the values are in fact equally spaced.

questions.solution_text:
Two of the four beads are marked $1$.
$P(X=1)=\frac{2}{4}$
$=\frac{1}{2}$
$P(X=2)=P(X=3)=\frac{1}{4}$
The probabilities are not all equal, so $X$ is not uniformly distributed.

questions.question_text:
A card is chosen at random from $24$ cards numbered $1$ to $24$, with every card equally likely.
Let $X$ be the number on the card.
Find $P(X\ge 19)$.

options.why: Excluded $19$, using $X>19$ instead of $X\ge 19$.
Counted the values from $1$ to $19$ instead of the values at least $19$.
Counted only $19$ instead of all six favourable values.

questions.solution_text:
Each of the $24$ values has probability $\frac{1}{24}$.
The favourable values are $19,\ 20,\ 21,\ 22,\ 23,\ 24$.
$P(X\ge 19)=\frac{6}{24}$
$=\frac{1}{4}$

questions.question_text:
Twelve cards numbered $1$ to $12$ are shuffled and one is drawn at random.
Let $X$ be the number on the card.
Find the probability that $X$ is a multiple of $4$.

options.why: Counted only $4$ and $8$, stopping before $12$.
Counted the even numbers instead of the multiples of $4$.
Counted the proper factors $1,\ 2,\ 3,\ 4,\ 6$ instead of multiples of $4$, and also omitted the factor $12$; all six factors would give $\frac{6}{12}$.

questions.solution_text:
Each card has probability $\frac{1}{12}$.
The multiples of $4$ from $1$ to $12$ are $4,\ 8,\ 12$, which is $3$ cards.
$P(X \text{ is a multiple of } 4)=\frac{3}{12}$
$=\frac{1}{4}$

questions.question_text:
A whole number from $17$ to $81$ inclusive is chosen, with every number equally likely.
Let $X$ be that number.
Find the probability that $X$ is a multiple of $9$.

options.why: Omitted $81$, counting only the seven multiples from $18$ to $72$.
Counted $81-17=64$ possible values instead of including both endpoints, giving $\frac{8}{64}$.
Included $9$ as a favourable value even though it is below the lower endpoint $17$.

questions.solution_text:
There are $81-17+1=65$ equally likely values.
The multiples of $9$ are $18,\ 27,\ 36,\ 45,\ 54,\ 63,\ 72,\ 81$, which is $8$ values.
$P(X\text{ is a multiple of }9)=\frac{8}{65}$
